chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:
A free woman is not compelled to breastfeed the child, while an umm al-walad is compelled to do so.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ: a bondwoman who has borne a child to her master
key_terms.الْحُرَّةُ: a free woman, as distinct from a slave woman
key_terms.الْوَلَدِ: the child or infant being nursed

ai.seo_question: Can a free woman be forced to breastfeed a child in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning breastfeeding obligations. It distinguishes between the free woman and the umm al-walad, stating that the former cannot be compelled to nurse the child while the latter can be compelled.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "A free woman cannot be forced to breastfeed a child, but a but a bondwoman (umm al-walad) can be compelled to do so."
